chapter.title: Before undocking · lunar orbit
chapter.startDescription: Eagle is still docked to Columbia. Armstrong and Aldrin prepare the LM; Collins remains in the CSM. The AGC is already operating. This chapter is a historical procedure reference, not a validated historical flight initial state.

timeline.title: Prepare Eagle while docked
timeline.crewRole: Commander and LM Pilot in Eagle; CM Pilot in Columbia
timeline.description: Review the pre-undocking checklist. Confirm the control configuration and crew responsibilities before release.

timeline.title: Undock and inspect Eagle
timeline.crewRole: LM crew maneuver; Collins inspects from Columbia
timeline.description: Undocking precedes visual inspection and the later CSM separation burn.

timeline.title: CSM separation maneuver
timeline.description: Columbia performs the separation maneuver; this is distinct from undocking.

timeline.title: Realign and prepare for DOI
timeline.description: Review P52 alignment and the DOI maneuver data before the burn.

timeline.title: Descent orbit insertion
timeline.description: Eagle fires its descent engine to lower perilune. Apollo 11 did not use the later mission sequence in which the CSM performs DOI before LM undocking.

timeline.title: P63 · prepare powered descent
timeline.description: Select and review the landing braking program with valid navigation, alignment, target, switch configuration, and ignition authorization.

timeline.title: Powered descent initiation
timeline.description: The descent engine ignites under the prepared P63 sequence.

timeline.title: P64 · approach and landing-site assessment
timeline.crewRole: Armstrong assesses terrain; Aldrin monitors and calls data
timeline.description: Approach guidance and pitchover expose the landing area. Landing-point redesignation is a mode-dependent use of the ACA.

timeline.title: P66 · commanded descent rate
timeline.crewRole: Commander controls attitude; LM Pilot calls flight data
timeline.description: ATT HOLD followed by ROD switch actuation enters P66. The crew commands attitude while the computer controls throttle to the selected descent rate.

timeline.title: Contact, shutdown, and landing checks
timeline.description: Distinguish contact indication, engine shutdown, and postlanding switch actions.

timeline.title: Surface operations · future chapter
timeline.crewRole: Armstrong and Aldrin on the surface; Collins in orbit
timeline.description: Landing checks precede preparation for EVA and surface work. This is a roadmap chapter, not implemented gameplay.

timeline.title: Lunar ascent · future chapter
timeline.description: The ascent stage leaves the descent stage on the Moon and returns toward lunar orbit. This is a roadmap chapter.

timeline.title: Rendezvous and docking · future chapter
timeline.crewRole: All three crew members in their respective spacecraft
timeline.description: Rendezvous, docking, and crew transfer precede Earth return. This is a roadmap chapter.

timeline.title: Earth return and entry · future chapter
timeline.crewRole: Three crew members reunited in Columbia
timeline.description: Trans-Earth injection, coast, command-module entry, and recovery complete the mission chronology. This is a roadmap chapter.

controls.label: ACA · attitude hand controller
controls.hardware: Right-hand pistol grip; spring-centered rotational controller
controls.location: Beside each crew station, right hand
controls.purpose: Change spacecraft orientation. Fore/aft commands pitch; left/right commands roll; twist commands yaw.

modes.label: PGNS ATT HOLD · rate command
modes.behavior: With the appropriate DAP and axis configuration, stick displacement requests angular rate and return to detent requests stabilization at the acquired attitude.

modes.label: Minimum impulse / pulse
modes.behavior: Pulse and direct paths depend on the axis switches, selected guidance system, and DSKY commands. They are not interchangeable with proportional rate command.

modes.label: P64 landing-point redesignation
modes.behavior: In the permitted approach mode, ACA inputs adjust the computer's landing target rather than acting as ordinary free steering.

controls.limitations: A browser pointer, keyboard, or gamepad is an input proxy. A two-axis yaw/pitch pad does not reproduce the ACA's pitch/roll/twist geometry, detents, hardover contacts, or all three independent axes. Exact live ACA behavior is not currently asserted.

controls.label: TTCA · thrust / translation controller
controls.hardware: Separate left-hand T-handle with THROTTLE / JETS selector
controls.location: Beside each crew station, left hand
controls.purpose: Command translation with RCS, or descent-engine thrust, according to selector and authority settings.

modes.label: JETS
modes.behavior: Translation along vehicle X, Y, and Z axes; this changes linear velocity rather than simply rotating the LM.

modes.label: THROTTLE
modes.behavior: Vertical handle travel controls descent thrust under the enabled throttle authority. The THR CONT switch and MAN THROT crew selector are separate controls.

controls.limitations: No current live TTCA translation/throttle contract is asserted. Do not turn a generic thrust slider into a claimed Apollo 11 hand controller.

controls.label: MODE CONTROL · PGNS
controls.hardware: Three-position toggle: AUTO / ATT HOLD / OFF

modes.label: AUTO
modes.behavior: Follow guidance attitude commands when the surrounding control configuration permits.

modes.label: ATT HOLD
modes.behavior: Permit the selected manual attitude-control mode. During landing, ATT HOLD plus a ROD actuation selects P66; ATT HOLD alone is not a universal P66 command.

modes.label: OFF
modes.behavior: Not a pause control. Changing guidance authority affects the spacecraft's control paths.

controls.limitations: Historical labels are inspectable reference information until a backend switch command, readback, and interlocks are implemented. AGS has a separate mode-control switch.

controls.label: ATTITUDE CONTROL · ROLL / PITCH / YAW
controls.hardware: One toggle per axis: MODE CONT / PULSE / DIR
controls.purpose: Select an axis control path independently of the PGNS / AGS mode toggles.

modes.label: MODE CONT
modes.behavior: Use the selected guidance-system mode for the axis.

modes.label: PULSE
modes.behavior: Use the pulse path appropriate to the selected guidance configuration.

modes.label: DIR
modes.behavior: Direct control is a distinct electrical path; it must not be emulated by bypassing the backend's validated command model.

controls.limitations: Not live switch controls. ACA/4 JET and TTCA/TRANSL ENABLE/DISABLE are additional separate switches.

controls.label: ROD · rate-of-descent switch
controls.location: Commander's left-hand control area, inboard of TTCA
controls.purpose: Adjust commanded vertical descent rate in P66; it does not directly prescribe a throttle percentage.

modes.label: P66 · computer throttle
modes.behavior: An up pulse reduces commanded descent rate by 1 ft/s; a down pulse increases it by 1 ft/s. The LGC computes the throttle response.

controls.limitations: Live ROD commands and P66 operation have not been exposed as a validated mission-control API.

controls.label: DSKY · display and keyboard
controls.hardware: Dedicated verb / noun keyboard and numeric registers
controls.purpose: Select programs, enter or review mission data, and respond to original software prompts.

modes.label: V37 · change major mode
modes.behavior: The original major-mode dispatcher validates and schedules the selected program; selecting P63 is one operation in an already initialized mission.

controls.limitations: A drawn keypad must remain unavailable unless real key delivery, release behavior, and original AGC readback are supported; never synthesize arbitrary key responses.

softwareEntry.summary: Luminary is scheduled, interrupt-driven flight software, not a linear mission script. The reset/restart entry, requested fresh start, idle P00, and selection of a mission program are different events. Start the lunar-orbit chapter with a validated running AGC checkpoint; do not present a fresh start or P63 selection as the beginning of Apollo 11.

files.meaning: Assembles source sections; it is not a game-style main() mission loop. Retained under docs/phase7-evidence/source/upstream/Luminary099/MAIN.agc.
The fixed interrupt/reset lead-in establishes the bank context and transfers to restart processing.
Requested fresh-start initialization. This is not a historical pre-undocking checklist step.
Major-mode selection and dispatch, with program table entries and execution scheduling.
P63 braking-program entry and ignition preparation require the mission state and alignment inputs; they do not reconstruct the previous mission.
Mode-dependent landing guidance and commanded vertical-rate processing. Its input discretes must come from authoritative cockpit state.
